subject: Energy
title: Ancient Water Mills
description: A 60-second lesson on Ancient Water Mills.

hook.text: Water mills appeared by the 3rd century BCE—harnessing flowing water to grind grain, replacing human labor.

buildup.text: The Roman Empire had thousands of water mills—the Barbegal complex in France had 16 wheels grinding flour.

discovery.text: Water wheels convert kinetic energy of flowing water into rotational power—a simple but revolutionary mechanism.

twist.text: By medieval times, mills powered sawmills, bellows, textile fulling, and hammers—not just grain grinding.

climax.text: The Domesday Book (1086) recorded over 6,000 water mills in England alone—one for every 300 people.

punchline.text: Flowing water turned wheels—mechanizing work centuries before steam.

quiz.question: How many water mills did the Domesday Book record in England?
